tickets.finding: THE DOGFOOD IS THE FINDING, and it took three runs to state honestly. (1) The acceptance command as written -- no declared partition -- reports unmappable and does NOT run the diff: consumable_as_architecture is false because lastCommand and result are written by all fifteen commands. Had the diff run, all 258 code edges would have been internal to the single component and the report would have read 0 divergences, 0 absences, coherent. (2) With a DECLARED four-component partition (surface / tickets / corpus / kill) the check runs and IS falsifiable: corpus<->kill and kill<->tickets have no port, so an edge across either would have been a divergence. 34 modules all mapped, 258 edges, 140 internal, 118 convergences, 0 divergences, 0 absences -- a genuine negative result about scripts/. The verdict is still unmappable, now for five extraction blind spots: three computed-name importlib.import_module calls, scripts/run_tlc.sh (no extractor), and spec_double_compiler/ (first-party, beside the code root, outside --code). (3) The COARSER three-component partition this ticket wrote first (folding kill_test in with the other scanner verdicts) has a port between every pair and could not have falsified anything; unfalsifiable_coherence fires and refuses to call it clean. Runs 2 and 3 are both defensible readings of the same model, separated by one variable's placement -- which is the ticket's central caution: the map and the partition are where the lying would happen, and the tool measures the declaration it is handed without being able to audit it. unfalsifiable_coherence catches only the fully degenerate case; a merely COARSE partition still reports a real-looking clean. Expect unmappable far more often than coherent on any real Python tree. Full write-up, including every way the tool looked wrong, noisy, or gameable, in the ticket's results/dogfood-findings.txt.
